Bill.BriefDescription: Prescribing license and trip permit fees for small trailers.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to small trailer license fees and trip permits;amending RCW 46.63.020; reenacting and amending RCW 46.16.0621; addingnew sections to chapter 46.16 RCW; creating a new section; andprescribing penalties.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 46.16.0621 and 2003 c 1 s 2 and 2002 c 352 s 7 areeach reenacted and amended to read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) License tab fees are required to be $30 per year for motorvehicles, regardless of year, value, make, or model. (2) For the purposes of this section, "license tab fees" aredefined as the general fees paid annually for licensing motor vehiclesand trailers as defined in RCW 46.04.620 and 46.04.623, including cars,sport utility vehicles, motorcycles, and motor homes. Trailerslicensed under RCW 46.16.068 or 46.16.085 or as provided for in section2 of this act and campers licensed under RCW 46.16.505 are not requiredto pay license tab fees under this section.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 46.16 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText:
In lieu of the fees provided in RCW 46.16.0621, trailers less thantwo thousand pounds scale weight and used for personal use on thepublic highways may be licensed upon the payment of a license feeaccording to the following weight schedule:
Under 250 pounds$0.00
250 1,999 pounds$30.00

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 46.16 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) The owner of a trailer that under reciprocal agreements withanother jurisdiction would be required to obtain a license registrationin this state or an unlicensed trailer that would be required to obtaina license registration for operation on public highways of this statemay, as an alternative to license registration, operate the trailerunder the authority of a trailer trip permit issued by this state. (2) Each trailer trip permit authorizes the operation of a singletrailer at the maximum legal weight limit for the vehicle for a periodof three consecutive days, commencing with the day of first use. Nomore than three such permits may be used for any one trailer in aperiod of thirty consecutive days. Every permit must identify, as thedepartment may require, the trailer for which it is issued and must becompleted in full and signed by the operator before use of the traileron the public highways. Correction of data on the permit such asdates, license number, or vehicle identification number invalidates thepermit. The trip permit must be displayed in the vehicle pulling thetrailer as prescribed by the department. (3) Trailers operating under the authority of trip permits aresubject to all laws, rules, and regulations affecting the operation oflike vehicles in this state. (4) Trailer trip permits may be obtained from field offices of thedepartment of transportation, Washington state patrol, department oflicensing, or other agents appointed by the department. The fee foreach trailer trip permit is three dollars and fifty cents. For eachpermit issued, a filing fee as provided by RCW 46.01.140 must becharged. The trailer trip permit fee must be deposited to the creditof the motor vehicle fund. These fees are in lieu of all other vehicle HB 1249 p. 2 license fees and taxes. No exchange, credits, or refunds may be givenfor trip permits after they have been purchased. (5) The department may appoint county auditors or businesses asagents for the purpose of selling trailer trip permits to the public.County auditors or businesses so appointed may retain the filing feecollected for each trip permit to defray expenses incurred in handlingand selling the permits. (6) A violation of or a failure to comply with any provision ofthis section is a gross misdemeanor. (7) The department of licensing may adopt rules as it deemsnecessary to administer this section.
